note: Engine line coverage ratchet. Gated buckets may not drop more than maxDropPct below `measured`. Measured over the HONEST combined surface: the unit lcov UNIONed with the Phase C in-process harness lcov (scripts/merge-coverage.ts). See docs/HARDENING-9-PLAN.md H-02.
targetNote:
target.lib=90 is the autonomous coverage campaign goal for the lib/ business-logic core. The gate measures the HONEST combined number: unit lcov UNIONed with the in-process harness lcov (scripts/merge-coverage.ts). Harness route suites (src/tests/harness/) plus focused unit tests climb toward 90%. External-service wiring (better-auth, S3, pg-boss, ioredis, Bun.SQL.subscribe, OTel SDK) + defensive catch-branches remain for integration/soak suites.

2026-07-15: measured.lib jumped 88.8 -> 96.7 WITHOUT new tests. This is not inflation. merge-coverage.ts stopped counting non-executable lines: bun's lcov emits DA records for // comments and blank lines and scores them hits=0, which across src/ charged 1663 comment + 1476 blank lines (92 of 157 files) to the denominator. Hit counts were unaffected; only the denominator dropped. The number now means what it says -- percent of EXECUTABLE lib lines covered. target.lib stays 90: it is met with real headroom, and the 0.5pt ratchet is what guards erosion from here.

2026-08-02: measured.lib 96.4 -> 98.0 and routes 72.7 -> 74.2 WITHOUT new tests, for the same reason as the 2026-07-15 jump and by the same mechanism. merge-coverage.ts stopped counting three more shapes bun emits DA records for but no test can execute: lines holding nothing but closing punctuation, continuation lines of a multi-line template literal, and members of an interface/type body. Measured before the change, across lib/ alone: of 561 lines the report called uncovered, 222 were closing punctuation, 78 were template continuations and 37 were type members -- 64% of the 'uncovered' figure was unreachable by any test. It also grew fastest on the code with the most explanation in it, which is a bad property for a number that decides whether a change may land. `} else {` and `} catch {` are deliberately still counted: they are control flow, and a never-taken branch there is a real gap. These numbers are measured on 8fcbf50 (the commit before the audit-remediation work) under the NEW filter, so the ratchet compares like with like: under it, that work moves lib -0.1pt and routes -0.2pt, both inside the 0.5pt allowance -- the 0.6pt 'regression' CI reported was entirely the measurement.

2026-08-19: measured.lib 98.0 -> 97.5. This is NOT a new measurement method and NOT a lowered bar to let a change through -- it is a stale record corrected to what the gate actually reads. The 98.0 was measured on 8fcbf50. Master has since measured 97.5 in its OWN CI (run 31673321737: lib 11848/12151 = 97.51%) and 97.5 again rebuilt locally from a clean worktree with its own install (11971/12281). Two independent measurements, one of them CI's, disagree with the recorded 98.0 by exactly 0.5 -- the entire allowance. The consequence: threshold = 98.0 - 0.5 = 97.5 and master = 97.5, so master sat precisely ON the failure boundary and ANY pull request costing even 0.1pt failed regardless of merit. The gate had stopped measuring drift-from-master and started measuring drift-from-a-number-nobody-could-reproduce. From 97.5 the ratchet has its intended 0.5pt of headroom back.

Two things were checked BEFORE touching this file, because the change unblocks the branch that made it and that is a conflict of interest. First, whether that branch actually erodes lib: measured on one machine, same filter, same procedure, clean runs both sides -- master 97.5 (11971/12281) vs branch 97.6 (12245/12548). The branch is 0.1pt ABOVE master, so the CI drop is the stale baseline, not the work. Second, whether more tests could close the gap: the remaining uncovered lines in the changed lib code hold nothing but string fragments of a multi-line expression, which no test can execute. bun distributes hits across such lines arbitrarily -- inside ONE console.warn in tenant-manager.ts, five consecutive lines scored 13 / 189 / 0 / 45 / 34, and a call executed once cannot have 189 hits on one line and 0 on the next. 418 such lines exist in lib (344 scored 'covered', 74 'uncovered'). Extending merge-coverage.ts to drop that shape WAS built and measured (lib: branch 98.1, master 98.0) and then DISCARDED: it moves routes as well (branch 73.0, master 74.0), so it cannot be compared against any recorded baseline, and a filter change cannot be validated in CI until it is already on master. That belongs in its own pull request, measured on master, not bundled into the one it would unblock.

measured.routes is deliberately NOT touched in the same pass, even though master measures above it too (CI 74.8 vs recorded 74.2). Raising it would tighten the gate on the basis of a number that is not stable: the same master tree measured routes 74.7 and then 75.5 locally depending only on whether DATABASE_URL was exported to the unit lane. routes currently passes, so there is nothing to fix under pressure -- and correcting only the bucket that blocks this branch while leaving the one that would tighten it is the shape of cherry-picking. It should be re-measured properly, on its own.
source: union of `bun test src/tests/unit --coverage` and `bun test src/tests/harness --coverage` lcovs via scripts/merge-coverage.ts (per-line DA hit union, non-executable lines excluded)
routesNote: `routes` is gated on the RATCHET with deliberately NO `target` entry. Rationale: every authz bug in this project's history landed in routes/ -- the 9 fixed in the security audit, the tenant-isolation campaign, the storage IDOR -- so the ratchet stops erosion where bugs actually happen. 2026-07-20: measured routes raised 59.7 -> 62.7 by adding in-process harness suites for insights (panels/shares/subscriptions), zones (pages/views/render), and approvals (submit/decide/cancel) -- 44 tests, which also surfaced+fixed two real 500s (insights share ON CONFLICT without a target; zones duplicate-slug now 409 not 500). Remaining routes gap is dominated by external-service wiring (backup=pg_dump/gzip/fs, realtime/ws/electric pub-sub, storage/media = S3) that belongs in integration/soak, not the harness -- so a hard `target` of 90 on routes is NOT reachable here and would block the 3.0.0 cut. Setting any real routes bar stays an OWNER call; until then the ratchet pins the floor. 2026-07-20 (second pass): raised further 62.7 -> 64.8 with harness suites for translations, tenants, users, permissions, import, revisions/comments -- 49 more tests, which surfaced+fixed a third duplicate-slug 500 (tenants POST now 409). Cumulative campaign 59.7 -> 64.8 (+5.1pt, 93 tests, 3 bugs). 2026-07-23 (third pass): 64.8 -> 67.1 by covering the *harness-reachable* slice of the external-service files — the real pg_dump/gzip backup create/status/download/delete + PITR path, media/storage folder+file DB-metadata CRUD and upload guards, and the realtime SSE auth gate. The residual is the genuinely un-harnessable I/O (S3 object bytes, SSE/ws stream fan-out, Electric) for integration/soak. 2026-07-23 (S3 lane): storage/media upload round-trip tests run against a SeaweedFS S3 endpoint (chrislusf/seaweedfs:3.68) when it is reachable, adding ~2.4pt locally and in CI; that also surfaced+fixed a 5th bug (media upload used a 21-char nanoid for a UUID id column, so every upload 500d). The endpoint is BEST-EFFORT — the ratchet floor stays the reproducible S3-free number (67.0) so the coverage gate is never hostage to external object-store infra. SSE/ws stream loops + Electric remain soak-only. 2026-07-24 (Phase A pass): 67.1 -> 68.6 (S3-free) by extending schema-branches (diff/review/reviews/preview enable-rotate-disable/soft-close-delete + error paths, 22.7 -> 58.2 on that file) and adding a first dedicated admin system-routes suite (status/field-types/types/schema/onboarding/stats/logs/slow-queries/revisions/api-keys/audit+CSV/notifications/migrate, 55.1 -> 67.3). The big remaining routes files are either already well-covered (collections has 22 suites, saved-queries is comprehensive) or external-service I/O whose real coverage lives in the OUT-OF-PROCESS integration lane (src/tests/integration/, not merged into this metric) -- so pushing this number to 90 needs those integration tests moved in-process with real services (the S3 lane pattern), NOT more harness happy-paths. Floor stays the reproducible S3-free number. 2026-07-24 (Phase A cont.): 68.6 -> 69.5 with dedicated suites for health.ts (58.8 -> 83.0) and routes/auth.ts (/api/me + the /api/invitations metadata/accept flow), plus foreign build artifacts (../sdk/dist/* — the SDK package's own compiled output) dropped from the metric in merge-coverage.ts (src-other 51.3 -> 39.0 as that now honestly reflects the engine's own index.ts bootstrap, not another package's dist). Remaining routes gap is the external-service files (ws/electric/backup/media/storage) whose coverage lives in the out-of-process integration lane -- a 3.1 Phase B (make S3 mandatory + move integration in-process). 2026-07-24 (Phase A finish): 69.5 -> 69.9 by extending saved-queries /execute over the applyFilter operators + filter-group/sort/pagination + preview-url branches (60.9 -> 74.9 on that file). Cumulative Phase A 67.1 -> 69.9 (+2.8pt, 5 suites). Phase B (S3-mandatory) was ATTEMPTED locally with a standalone SeaweedFS (weed 3.68, no docker needed) matching the CI env exactly, but the storage/media S3 upload round-trip still times out (aws4fetch<->SeaweedFS handshake is setup-fragile) -- confirming the best-effort lane decision; making it a hard gate needs that handshake debugged first, so the floor stays S3-free.
